scope: Local animated-diffuse guide split; no radiance/path-tracing, sample-budget, spatial strength or motion-threshold changes.

discovery.diagnosis: The initial +0.875 guide preserved both direct analytic projection and noisy stationary theater surfaces exactly, so the actual show case produced identical raw and reconstructed images.

conditions: Stationary hit within 14 m of projection center
No thin-sheet transmission before the hit
classification.policy: Reject temporal history; retain existing current-frame edge-aware spatial filter. Traffic strong reactivity has priority.
classification.preserved: Direct screen, local emitters, smooth/metallic surfaces, transmission and traffic retain current coverage.

actualGPUGuideChecks: Unrelated distant surface, behind-facing mirror and sphere-missing mirror retain original guides

reconstructionFixture.input: Two independent deterministic noisy current-radiance fields with changing analytic panel illumination, shared planar geometry, a contrasting material/albedo boundary, and compatible stale prior color. Actual production temporal and three spatial GPU passes.

negativeControls.change: Remove only the +0.25 temporal rejection condition from the actual shader
negativeControls.result: Compatible stale historical illumination blends into current RGB

negativeControls.change: Use the preceding +0.875 classification on the same noisy input
negativeControls.result: Temporal and spatial outputs are exactly raw, reproducing zero reconstruction improvement

sharedRegression: All existing GPU denoiser checks pass, including traffic, sky, emitter, thin iron, normal/depth/material/albedo edges, glass, night-window mixed coverage, glossy temporal history and dim reflected-detail guards.
limitations: Synthetic reconstruction noise reduction is not a full-world improvement or frame-rate claim.
Old-guide equality is controlled GPU equality; independent whole-world acceleration structures are not asserted bit-identical.
Final full-world 26-case release run is separate and pending when this report is written.
The local radius and first-reflection guide do not classify every rough or multiple-bounce illumination path.
